hook_location: output of model.model.layers[14] (residual stream after that decoder block)
token_selection: every non-padding token, per the attention mask
special_token_handling: Qwen3 tokenizer has no bos_token; plain tokenizer(text) calls add no BOS/EOS automatically (verified empirically) -- every retained token id is a real content token, not a special token, under this protocol
truncation_policy: no truncation applied -- corpus max tokenized length (266) is far below the model's max_position_embeddings (40960); --max-length is supported in the pipeline but left unset for this run

batching.strategy: length-bucketed: prompts sorted by tokenized length before batching, so each batch pads only to the longest prompt within that batch
batching.padding_side: right (required for correctness with a causal model doing a single non-generation forward pass)

storage_format.format: safetensors shards (one tensor named "activations", shape [n_rows, 2048], dtype bfloat16)
storage_format.rationale: safetensors natively supports bfloat16 (numpy .npy does not), supports fast memory-mapped reads via safe_open without loading a whole shard into RAM, and is already the format used for this project's model weights -- no new dependency. A prompt's tokens are never split across two shards (a shard is flushed before it would overflow), keeping resumption/validation simple.

train_validation_split.level: prompt (all tokens from a prompt stay in the same split)
train_validation_split.method: sha256(f'{seed}:{prompt_id}') -> deterministic pseudo-random fraction in [0,1), < val_fraction => validation

resumability.verification: a prompt counts as complete only if every shard its rows belong to is marked status=complete in shard_manifest.json AND that shard file's sha256 on disk matches the manifest -- re-verified at the start of every run, not just trusted from the manifest
